title: Watching the dispatcher: what it started, what it is holding, what broke
description:
The dispatcher from the node above runs unattended, which means by default nobody sees it work. Today the only live views are per node — `sober run <node> --watch` follows one agent, `sober logs <node>` reads the last run — and `sober dashboard` serves the board without a queue view. There is no surface that answers "what has it started since I left, and what is it refusing to start".

`runQueue` already returns exactly that shape and it is currently thrown away outside `drain`: `started`, `dispatched` one-per-started, and `held` — each held node with a `why` string already written for a human ("x, y are heading for the same files", "someone has claimed it"). The work is carrying it to a surface, not computing it.

What it shows, per cycle: what started and on which base, what finished and how, what is held and why, and what the concurrency limit is currently refusing. A held node is the important half — an unattended queue that is quietly holding four nodes for a reason nobody reads is worse than one that stopped.

Acceptance: with the dispatcher running, the watch surface shows a node moving from held to started to finished without a restart; a held node shows the same `why` the drain prints today; and closing the watch does not stop the dispatcher. Tests beside the code.
